reasoning: Idaho’s statewide structural lean is strongly Republican, with a Cook PVI of R+27. For the current 2026 Senate race, the freshest credible items in the last 45 days do not provide a traditional state-general-election poll average, but reporting and a June statewide poll show Sen. Jim Risch leading by a very large margin; the best current read from the available evidence is a Republican advantage well into the mid-30s to 40-point range.

sources.name: Peak Insights poll via Prediction Hunt
sources.details: Statewide poll found Jim Risch at 55%, Democrat David Roth at 15%, with other candidates and undecideds splitting the rest; this implies a 40-point Republican lead.

sources.name: Achilles-sponsored poll via ABC45
sources.details: Reported that an Achilles-sponsored poll placed independent Todd Achilles within four points of Risch in a hypothetical one-on-one matchup, though nearly a quarter of voters were undecided; because it is a sponsor-reported spring poll and not a current general-election result, it is treated cautiously.

sources.name: Bullfinch Group poll via The Downballot
sources.details: Reported an early June Bullfinch Group poll showing Risch with a 40-36 edge over Achilles in a hypothetical one-on-one matchup and 41-18 in a three-way contest with Roth; the one-on-one result implies a 4-point Republican lead.

sources.name: Roll Call report on Roth dropout
sources.details: Reported that Democrat David Roth dropped out, leaving independent Todd Achilles as the main challenger to Republican Sen. Jim Risch; this is context, not a margin poll.
